name: @godxjp/ui-mcp

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List every design/taste skill bundled by this MCP (id + name + whenToUse + section ids). Use FIRST to discover skills; then `get_skill_section` to drill in.

tools.name: list_primitives
tools.description: List every @godxjp/ui primitive/composite/shell (group + tagline per entry). Optionally filter by group. Then `get_component` for one's full API. Core only by default — pass tier="lab" for the opt-in @godxjp/ui/lab components.

tier.description: Default "core". "lab" lists the opt-in `@godxjp/ui/lab` components (niche, kept and tested, not in the default context); "all" lists both.

tools.name: list_utilities
tools.description: List every NON-component public export of @godxjp/ui — hooks, helper functions and constants (cn, formatDate, formatCurrency, toast, useDebouncedValue, buttonVariants, CHART_COLORS, SHOW_PARENT …). Reach for this before hand-writing a className merger, a date/money formatter, a debounce hook or a chart palette: two products in this org each re-implemented `cn` because it could not be found. Optionally filter by kind. Then `get_component name="<name>"` for its signature, usage and example.

kind.description: hook = only legal inside a component body; function = callable anywhere; value = a constant to read.

tools.name: list_patterns
tools.description: List every canonical copy-paste code pattern (signup-form, settings-page, data-table-page, async-data-state, confirm-destructive, …); common aliases resolve too. Use before `get_pattern`.

tools.name: list_anti_ai_tells
tools.description: List every AI-tell pattern to AVOID (optionally by category). Use to self-audit a design before shipping; then `get_anti_ai_tell` for the fix.

tools.name: list_redesign_checks
tools.description: List the redesign audit checklist (50+ checks; optionally by category). Use when auditing an existing project; then `get_redesign_check` for a symptom's fix.

tools.name: list_audit_rules
tools.description: List the LOCAL static ui-audit rules (scripts/ui-audit.mjs) to run BEFORE any visual review — each cites the standard it enforces (WCAG/WAI-ARIA/Intl/ISO/IANA/CSS-Logical) + a fix + the run command. Optionally by category.

tools.name: list_visual_checks
tools.description: List the RUNTIME visual-audit checks (scripts/visual-audit.mjs — Playwright + axe-core) to run against the RUNNING app: contrast/ARIA (axe), target size, rendered-accent chroma, DOM emoji, banner layout. Needs a browser (vs list_audit_rules, static). Optionally by category.

tools.name: get_anti_ai_tell
tools.description: Fetch ONE anti-AI-tell — full body + concrete fix. Use after `list_anti_ai_tells`.

tools.name: get_redesign_check
tools.description: Fetch redesign check(s) matching a symptom snippet. Returns full fix + UI note. Use after `list_redesign_checks`.

symptom.description: Fragment of the symptom text (e.g. 'Inter everywhere' / '100vh').

tools.name: get_skill_section
tools.description: Fetch ONE section of ONE skill — token-efficient. E.g. `skill='soft', section='double-bezel'`. Use after `list_skills` narrowed the relevant skill + section.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Full guide for one @godxjp/ui component — import path, props/types/defaults, HOW to use it (DO/DON'T), WHEN to reach for it (use cases), related components (don't reinvent/confuse), a copy-paste example, story path, and cardinal rules. Use this before hand-rolling anything. Design-token knobs are listed compactly (name+default); pass `verbose:true` for what each token controls.

verbose.description: Include the full design-token table with a 'what it controls' description per token. Default false (compact token+default only) to save context.

tools.name: get_pattern
tools.description: Full code snippet for one canonical pattern — copy-paste-ready.

tools.name: get_rule
tools.description: Read one cardinal rule from CLAUDE.md (by number) OR all if no number.

tools.name: get_vocab
tools.description: Read shared prop-vocabulary type (`SizeProp`, `StatusProp`, `ColorProp`, `LoadingProp`, etc.) OR all if no name.

tools.name: get_tokens
tools.description: Read design tokens, optionally filtered by tier category (primitive / semantic / component).

tools.name: list_consumer_skills
tools.description: List the design skills relevant to an app-dev BUILDING WITH @godxjp/ui (audience consumer/both). Hides core library-maintenance skills. START HERE if you import @godxjp/ui and want guidance (design-to-page, compose-a-screen, taste, …). Returns id + name + whenToUse + section ids.

tools.name: get_consumer_skill
tools.description: Fetch ONE section of ONE consumer-facing skill. Same as get_skill_section but refuses core-only skills (steers app-devs away from library-maintenance material). Use after list_consumer_skills / route_consumer_task.

tools.name: route_consumer_task
tools.description: Natural-language task → consumer skill+section pointer. Like route_task but only points to consumer-facing skills (never core library-maintenance). Use FIRST when you're building an app with @godxjp/ui.

task.description: Describe what you want to build.

tools.name: draft_bug_report
tools.description: When @godxjp/ui ITSELF is at fault (missing token, a primitive lacking the controlled-vocabulary prop, a real a11y/behaviour bug, a wrong catalog example) and you cannot follow a rule — DON'T fake a workaround. This drafts a detailed GitHub issue body + a copy-paste `gh issue create` command so you can report it. Prints the command only; never runs gh.

summary.description: One-line title of the bug / blocked rule.

repro.description: Minimal steps or code to reproduce.

component.description: Affected component name, if any (links to get_component).

rule.description: Cardinal rule number that can't be followed, if any.

tools.name: check_compatibility
tools.description: Report whether the @godxjp/ui version installed in the target project matches THIS catalog (which describes one release train). A mismatched minor means the props/tokens/patterns may describe a build they never installed (#140). Pass the installed version (`npm ls @godxjp/ui`); call it at the START of a consumer session.

version.description: Installed @godxjp/ui version in the target project, e.g. '16.10.0'. Omit to just read the catalog's own version + compatible range.

tools.name: route_task
tools.description: Natural-language task → skill+section pointer (e.g. 'design a premium agency hero' → soft/vibe-archetypes). Use FIRST when you don't know which skill applies.

task.description: Describe what you want to build.

tools.name: suggest_primitive
tools.description: Use case → primitive recommendation. E.g. 'confirm a destructive delete' → DangerZone pattern + Dialog suggestion.

tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Fuzzy-search primitives by name / tagline / prop. Returns ranked matches. Core only by default; pass tier="lab" or "all" to include the opt-in @godxjp/ui/lab components.

tier.description: Default "core". "lab" lists the opt-in `@godxjp/ui/lab` components (niche, kept and tested, not in the default context); "all" lists both.

tools.name: get_frame_coverage
tools.description: Verified preview-contract coverage for a component (issue #163). Answers 'is this state actually PROVEN?' — returns, per contract dimension (variants, tones, sizes, shapes, density, controlled/uncontrolled ownership, disabled/read-only/loading/empty/error/success, async retry/cancel/offline, responsive viewport matrix, RTL, long/localized content, keyboard/focus, accessible name/description/error, reduced motion / coarse touch), whether an EXECUTED case proves it (covered), whether nothing proves it (UNTESTED), or whether it cannot exist (not-applicable, with a reason). UNTESTED IS NOT A PASS: never infer that a component supports a state because an example renders. Call this before telling a user a component 'supports' anything. Omit `name` for the repo-wide summary and the tracked known gaps.

name.description: Public export name (e.g. 'Button', 'DataTable', 'CardFooter'). Omit for the repo-wide coverage summary.

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: DESIGN.md — the visual spec for screens built with @godxjp/ui: real tokens (YAML front matter), colour scarcity rules, typography, layout & density, elevation, components, ADMIN SCREEN ANATOMY (list / detail / form / settings / dashboard / approval queue), do's and don'ts, responsive, iteration guide, known gaps. Read before composing a screen. Pass `section` for one section; omit it for the whole document (~12 KB).

section.description: Section id or heading word, e.g. 'tokens', 'colors', 'admin-screen-anatomy', 'dos-and-donts', 'iteration-guide'. Unknown ids list the valid ones.

tools.name: get_exemplar
tools.description: A reference screen to match for an admin archetype: its anatomy notes from DESIGN.md, the full source of the showcase built from real @godxjp/ui primitives, and its live preview URL for screenshot comparison. Archetypes: list, detail, editor, reader, settings, dashboard, approval-queue. Omit `archetype` to list them.

archetype.description: list | detail | editor | reader | settings | dashboard | approval-queue (aliases: index, table, crud, collection, 一覧, record, show, master-detail, 詳細, form, edit, create, document-editor, record-editor, 編集, document, article, wiki, view, read, 閲覧, preferences, account, 設定, overview, home, kpi, ダッシュボード, approval, queue, inbox, review, 承認).

tools.name: lint_jsx
tools.description: Heuristic check of a JSX snippet for common violations — raw `<button>` / `<input>`, `color='error'` on Tag/Badge, missing aria-label, missing source.code override on stories with cell renderers (rule 34), etc.

instructions:
Building UI with @godxjp/ui. Before any JSX:
1. get_design — DESIGN.md: tokens, scarcity rules, screen anatomy, do/don't.
2. route_consumer_task → compose-a-screen for app screens (marketing skills are for landing pages only).
3. get_exemplar for the closest archetype (no argument lists them: list, detail, editor, reader, settings, dashboard, approval-queue) — match its structure.
4. search_components before get_component; never guess a prop.
After building: ui-audit at zero errors, then run `npx @godxjp/ui visual-audit <url> <routes>` (320/390/768/1024/1280/844×390) to zero machine failures, inspect every screenshot at every width region by region (including regions you must not change), no top-N or round cap; report "probes passed; independent acceptance pending" — never accept your own screen.
